newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed's new alliance widens rifts in Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Lebed's new alliance widens rifts in Kremlin.

text.p: Security tsar Alexander Lebed has widened a rift with his rivals in the Kremlin by forging a liaison with President Boris Yeltsin's former bodyguard which analysts say has deeply alarmed his opponents.

Lebed gave up trying to conceal his informal alliance with the shadowy Alexander Korzhakov, one of Yeltsin's inner circle and a confidant for more than a decade, when he publicly backed his new friend's bid to run for parliament on Sunday.

Lebed, who has one of the cleanest images in Russian politics, is joining forces with one whose name is almost synomynous with political intrigues in order to widen his power base and gain an experienced counsellor in an area in which he is a novice.
Independent analysts say presidential chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais is deeply concerned by the alliance between his two rivals.

They say Chubais encouraged a campaign of mudslinging against Korzhakov last week which added a new ferocity to the power struggle under way as Yeltsin prepares for heart surgery. The chances of compromise between Chubais and Lebed look bleak.

"This alliance is clearly a move by Lebed in his fight with Chubais and the more they get into conflict, the less chance there is of a compromise," Viktor Kremenyuk, an analyst at the independent U.S.A. and Canada thinktank, told Reuters.
"Lebed is keen to get some support among the power circles which Korzhakov long had control of. Also, he is isolated in the Kremlin and needs someone to guide him."
Yeltsin brought Lebed, 46, into the Kremlin last June as a vote-winning move after the former paratroop general came third in the first round of a presidential election.
Korzhakov was ousted as head of presidential security two days later with other hardliners. The purge was seen as a victory for Chubais and Kremlin liberals.

Yeltsin went on to defeat his communist challenger in the second round but has been out of the Kremlin with heart trouble for most of the time since then. His doctors say he likely to have surgery in the next two months.
Russian analysts say the gruff national security adviser has been locked in battle with Chubais since the liberal former privatisation guru became head of Yeltsin's administration in July.
Lebed does not hide his desire to become president and would be in a strong position if an early election were called because Yeltsin proved unable to govern.

Chubais has no immediate presidential ambitions. But his position and that of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who has been handed some of Yeltsin's powers temporarily, would be threatened by an early election.
The liaison with Korzhakov extends Lebed's sphere of influence and could gain him access to the riches some newspapers say the hawkish aide has piled up.
It also gives Lebed a measure of control over the compromising material which Korzhakov says he has stacked up over the years and which could be a powerful weapon in the power struggle.
"This is part of Lebed's efforts to find quick solutions in his power struggle. Time is money for him and he has to find partners," political analyst Lilia Shevtsova said.
"It is clear Chubais has launched a desparate struggle against Lebed and he has powerful groups behind him which regard Lebed as a big danger."
She was referring to elite financial groups whose influence would be threatened if Lebed came to power.

She and Kremenyuk said Lebed appeared also to be strengthening his ties with Korzhakov to win over any supporters still remaining in the Kremlin's security forces and administration in case the power struggle became violent.
"If there are no elections, there are other routes to power. These people could be important to Lebed," Shevtsova said.
The liaison with Korzhakov also entails dangers for Lebed.

Korzhakov was accused by a former top businessman last week of trying to extort millions of dollars from him. Korzhakov denied the charge, but Lebed risks tarnishing his image by supporting his bid to enter parliament.

For his part, Korzhakov could regard parliamentary immunity as useful protection if he faces a legal investigation but he also sees Lebed as a powerful ally to help him come out of the shadows and start a political career.
